memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "All these blessings will come on you and accompany you if you obey the Lord your God: You will be blessed in the city and blessed in the country. The fruit of your womb will be blessed, and the crops of your land and the young of your livestock — the calves of your herds and the lambs of your flocks." — Deut 28:2-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God promised Israel that His blessings would "come on you and accompany you" — even overtake you, as some translations put it. The picture is of blessing chasing the obedient down and catching up with them. City and country, family and fields, herds and flocks — every corner of life would flourish under God's favour. For an agricultural nation about to enter a new land, this was deeply reassuring.

Again, we must not turn this into a promise of guaranteed wealth for believers today. These were covenant blessings for national Israel, tied to the land God was giving them. But behind the specific promises stands the unchanging character of a generous God. Our God is not stingy. He delights to bless His people, and every good gift still comes down from Him (Jas 1:17).

The greatest blessings God gives us in Christ are not calves and crops, but forgiveness, adoption, His presence, His Spirit, and eternal life. Paul says God has blessed us "with every spiritual blessing in Christ" (Eph 1:3). These blessings truly do overtake us — not because we earned them, but because of grace.

So when you count your blessings, look beyond the material. See the good hand of a generous Father who has poured out His richest gifts on you through His Son.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I see God as generous, or as reluctant to bless?
2. Am I counting the spiritual blessings I have in Christ, not just material ones?
3. How can I thank God today for a blessing that has "overtaken" me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Generous Father, thank You for being lavish in Your goodness toward me. Help me treasure above all the spiritual blessings I have in Christ, and to live grateful. Amen.
